title: Study plan
description: Discover subjects, structure, exams, teaching approach and much more of the Master in Oncology, Translational Immunology and Aging offered by USI.

blocks.html:
Overview

The Master’s programme equips students with the scientific knowledge and practical skills needed to investigate the molecular and cellular basis of human disease, with a particular focus on oncology, immunology, and aging.

Extensive laboratory training also takes place in the leading-edge laboratories of the Bios⁺ research campus in Bellinzona.

Study plan

The study plan and course descriptions provide an overview of the programme’s structure and content, and may be subject to changes.

Enrolled students should refer to the GESTU platform, where they can access the course offering, updated progressively each semester.

View Study plan (PDF)

items.title: Research Groups
items.html:
During the third and fourth semesters, students undertake their thesis whilst working in an IRB, IOR or IRT laboratory. A list of the laboratories currently in operation is provided below.

Alimonti Andrea

The Alimonti Research Group (Molecular Oncology, IOR) investigates the cellular and molecular mechanisms that drive cancer progression, with a particular focus on cellular senescence, aging, tumor–immune interactions, and prostate cancer. A major research area explores how senescent cells and their microenvironment influence tumor growth, immune surveillance, and response to therapy. A second area focuses on developing innovative strategies to selectively target senescent and cancer cells and to restore effective anti-tumor immunity. The ultimate goal is to translate fundamental discoveries in senescence and cancer biology into new therapeutic approaches for cancer and age-related disease.

Baggiolini Arianna

The Baggiolini Research Group (Stem Cells and Cancer, IOR) investigates the mechanisms underlying oncogenic competence, from cellular state and lineage specificity to the tumour microenvironment. The laboratory has a special interest in the neural tumour microenvironment and its impact on tumour initiation and progression. To pursue these questions, we develop and employ human pluripotent stem cell-based models of human tissues and organs, including neural tissue.

Barile Lucio

The Barile Research Group (Cardiovascular Theranostics Group, IRT) investigates two main research areas. The first focuses on the role of cellular senescence in cardiovascular diseases, exploring the molecular mechanisms through which senescent cardiovascular cells contribute to cardiac ageing, pathological remodelling, and the development of heart failure. The second explores the use of extracellular vesicles (EVs) as a liquid biopsy in cardiovascular disease, aiming to identify circulating EV signatures that can provide novel diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers and improve cardiovascular risk stratification and disease monitoring.

Bersini Simone

The Bersini Research Group (Vascular Aging, IRT) exploits biofabrication technologies to develop 3D miniaturized models of human perfusable blood vessels integrated within organ-specific microenvironments. These high-throughput organs-on-a-chip are employed to answer disease-relevant questions mainly in the field of aging and age-related diseases (including cancer) with the goal to identify key mechanisms underlying blood vessel aging and exploit them in the field of regenerative medicine.

Bertoni Francesco

The Lymphoma Genomics Lab (Bertoni group, IOR) focuses on lymphoma genomics and the development of novel anti-lymphoma therapies. We combine genomic approaches with bioinformatic and functional studies to identify molecular lesions sustaining lymphoma cells, mechanisms of drug resistance, and novel therapeutic targets. Our ultimate goal is to translate biological discoveries into improved treatments for patients. We collaborate closely with academic groups and pharmaceutical companies. Partnerships with the International Extranodal Lymphoma Study Group (IELSG), Oncology Institute of Southern Switzerland (IOSI), and Swiss Cancer Institute facilitate the translation of preclinical findings into clinical studies.

Calcinotto Arianna

The Calcinotto Research Group (Cancer Immunotherapy, IOR) investigates the complex interactions between the immune system and cancer. One major research area focuses on understanding how neutrophils and other immune cells are reprogrammed within the tumor microenvironment to promote cancer initiation, progression, and resistance to therapy. A second area explores how systemic and microenvironmental factors, including metabolites and the microbiome, shape immune cell function and influence tumor development and therapeutic response. The ultimate goal is to identify new immune mechanisms that can be exploited for cancer prevention and treatment.

Carbone Giuseppina

The Prostate Cancer Biology Lab (Carbone group, IOR) investigates the molecular mechanisms that drive prostate cancer progression, lineage plasticity, and therapy resistance. We study how transcription factors and epigenetic regulators reshape cancer cell identity and promote the emergence of aggressive castration-resistant and neuroendocrine prostate cancer. We explore innovative therapeutic strategies, including transcriptional reprogramming, RNA-based approaches, and targeted treatments, to restore epithelial differentiation, suppress cancer stemness, and prevent metastasis. Our goal is to translate these discoveries into precision therapies for patients with advanced prostate cancer. Learn more about our research projects on the official IOR website.

Catapano Carlo

The Catapano Laboratory (Experimental Therapeutics, IOR) investigates innovative cancer treatment strategies by dissecting the interplay between epigenetic, transcriptional, and metabolic processes that drive cancer evolution, stemness, metastasis, and treatment resistance. Our research aims to identify key biological mechanisms and actionable molecular targets for novel therapeutic approaches. Using clinically relevant preclinical models, we evaluate small-molecule compounds, RNA and DNA therapeutics, antibody-based therapeutics, and nanoparticle delivery systems to develop next-generation therapeutic payloads and delivery strategies that address the biological and phenotypic complexity of human cancers. Project descriptions are available on the Catapano Lab website.

Cejka Petr

The Cejka Research Group (Recombination Mechanisms, IRB), investigates the molecular mechanisms that maintain genome stability. One major area focuses on the repair of DNA double-strand breaks by homologous recombination, including the mechanisms that process broken DNA ends and regulate the choice between different DNA repair pathways. A second area explores how DNA repair and replication proteins act on challenging DNA structures, including repetitive DNA sequences, with the aim of understanding the mechanisms underlying trinucleotide repeat instability and meiotic recombination.

Cereghetti Gea

The Cereghetti Research Group (Protein Self-Organization Laboratory, IRB) investigates how proteins self-organize into biomolecular condensates and amyloid assemblies, and how these processes regulate cellular functions in health and disease. We combine cell biology, biochemistry, biophysics, and microfluidics to uncover the roles of protein self-organization in immunity, aging, and neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s.

Geiger Roger

The Geiger lab investigates how cellular metabolism and signaling regulate T-cell function. We combine immunology, systems biology, and genetic engineering to uncover mechanisms controlling antitumor immunity and develop improved T-cell therapies. Our work includes functional CRISPR screening, T-cell receptor specificity, and synthetic biology approaches for cancer immunotherapy.

González F. Santiago

The Infection and Immunity lab at the IRB (https://irb.usi.ch/infection-and-immunity/) investigates host-pathogen interactions during respiratory viral and bacterial infections. They analyze immune cell dynamics and inflammation using advanced 2-photon intravital microscopy. In addition, their research explores how the inflammatory reaction impact both infectious disease and cancer.

Guarda Greta

The Guarda Research Group (Immune Mechanisms, IRB) investigates two main areas. The first one focuses on the interaction between cytotoxic T cells and cancer cells, regulated by antigen presentation and immune checkpoint molecules. The second one explores the mechanisms controlling the metabolic activation of immune cells, a process that is essential for immune responses but also for cancer development.

Molinari Maurizio

The Molinari Research Group (protein folding and quality control, IRB) investigates how cells preserve protein and organelle homeostasis. We focus on protein folding, quality control and degradation in endoplasmic reticulum, with particular emphasis on ER-associated degradation, ER-phagy and ER-to-lysosome-associated degradation. We use cell biology, biochemistry, and imaging to uncover mechanisms relevant to proteopathies, infection and therapy.

Monticelli Silvia

The Monticelli Research Group (Molecular Immunology, IRB) investigates how T lymphocytes are regulated at the molecular level. One area of research focuses on post-transcriptional regulation mediated by RNA-binding proteins, to determine how stimulus-induced responses can be modulated. We are also interested in understanding how specific genetic factors may predispose individuals to develop autoimmune diseases.

Nobs Samuel

The Nobs Research Group Microbiome Immune Interactions, IRB investigates the role of the microbiome and how it influences the immune system. We are particularly interested in studying the specific molecular mechanisms by which microbes influence respiratory health and disease including viral and bacterial infections as well as chronic lung diseases such as idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and asthma.

Robbiani Davide

The Immunology and infectious disease lab (Robbiani, IRB Bios+) studies B lymphocytes, which produce antibodies essential for immune defense and vaccine efficacy. It investigates serologic determinants of disease severity, particularly autoantibodies targeting immune factors, and conducts translational research on emerging infections and diseases affecting immunosuppressed individuals, pregnancies and older adults.

Rossi Davide

The Rossi Research Group (Experimental Hematology Lab, IOR ) focuses on the molecular pathogenesis of lymphoma and chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). We translate genomic discoveries into clinical biomarkers to improve diagnosis, prognostic stratification, and treatment of mature B-cell tumors. In CLL, we identify markers predicting response to novel targeted therapies. We also validate liquid biopsy approaches using cell-free DNA and ultra-deep next-generation sequencing to enable real-time tumor genotyping, diagnosis, prognostication, and treatment monitoring in mature B-cell malignancies.

Varani Luca

Luca Varani's Structural Biology group studies how antibodies neutralize pathogens by combining wet-lab experiments and computational biology. Focusing mainly on infectious diseases like Flaviviruses, Coronaviruses, and Prions, we use a multidisciplinary approach to engineer new antibodies in different formats (specializing in multispecific designs) with improved activity or with functions
